title: Calvin vs Gordon: tuition, size, location
summary: Calvin University (Calvin) versus Gordon College (Gordon). Also searched as Gordon vs Calvin. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Gordon College and Calvin University are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Gordon College, located in Wenham, has an undergraduate enrollment of 1,278 students, whereas Calvin University in Grand Rapids enrolls 3,193 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at Gordon College is $30,700, which is lower compared to Calvin University's in-state tuition of $39,350. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between Gordon vs Calvin.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Gordon College and Calvin University show notable differences. Gordon College charges $30,700 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, while Calvin University’s tuition is higher at $39,350 for both categories. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who completed their programs at Gordon College is $26,250, which exceeds Calvin University’s median debt of $23,250. These figures illustrate that Gordon vs Calvin differ in tuition fees and median debt levels, with Gordon offering lower tuition but higher median debt among completers.
